findings.summary: gh_api() has no --max-time bound, unlike both gitea_api branches.
findings.mechanism: The task brief calls for bounding how long any single request can run; gitea_api got --max-time 1800/60 but the gh_api curl invocation (lines 55-60) was left with no timeout at all, so a hung/stalled connection to api.github.com during the enumeration loop can block indefinitely despite the stated goal of bounding every request.

findings.summary: BODY_FILE is not truncated when curl fails before starting output, so error messages can report a stale body from a previous call.
findings.mechanism: curl -o only (re)writes the file once it begins receiving a response; on a connection-level failure (DNS/connect/timeout — the exact case this diff is now supposed to tolerate) curl exits nonzero without writing to $BODY_FILE, leaving the previous call's response body in place. Verified: `curl -o file -w '%{http_code}' http://nonexistent.invalid.domain.test/` prints http_code 000 but leaves file contents untouched. Since status is correctly caught as empty/000 and reported, but body_msg() then reads the stale file, callers (e.g. `die "GitHub API error ... $(body_msg)"` at line 124, or the migrate failure message at line 168) can print an unrelated error message from an earlier successful/failed request instead of reflecting the actual network failure.
